request.prompt: Which humanoid robots have SDK access?

result.text:
As of November 2026, several commercially available humanoid robots offer developer SDKs, APIs, or ROS 2 interfaces. The strongest options depend on whether you want to develop applications, control joints, build autonomous behaviors, or train your own AI models.

The important distinction is between:

Open SDK: Public documentation and development libraries.

ROS 2 access: Integration with the standard robotics middleware ecosystem.

Low-level control: Direct access to motors, joints, sensors and actuators.

Cloud API: Remote control through a manufacturer's platform.

Research access: Development interfaces available through partnerships or research agreements.

Humanoid robots with developer SDKs

1. Unitree G1

Public SDK

Python and C++ SDKs

ROS 2 support

Joint and motion control

Reinforcement learning and simulation

Open-source developer repositories

Documentation: Unitree SDK · GitHub

2. Unitree H1 / H2

Public SDK

Python and C++ interfaces

ROS 2

Low-level motor control

Locomotion and motion-control development

Simulation integration

Documentation: Unitree developer documentation

3. Booster T1 / T2

Public SDK

Python SDK

C++ SDK

DDS-based communication

ROS 2 interoperability

Joint, trajectory and motion control

Sensor and camera data access

Documentation: Python SDK · C++ SDK

4. LimX Oli

Public SDK

Full Python development

Modular SDK

High- and low-level interfaces

URDF model

Joint and end-effector control

AI and reinforcement-learning research

Documentation: Oli developer FAQ · Documentation center

5. AGIBOT X2

Public SDK

AimDK development platform

Downloadable SDK

URDF models

ROS-based development

Education and research configurations

Documentation: AimDK X2 SDK

These have published development support, although access conditions and the extent of publicly available documentation vary.

Robots without publicly documented general-purpose SDKs

These are notable platforms, but I would not assume unrestricted third-party development access:

Tesla Optimus

Boston Dynamics Atlas

1X NEO

Figure 03

Agility Digit

This means no publicly documented general-purpose SDK comparable to Unitree's, not necessarily that manufacturer or research-partner access is impossible.

My recommendation

If your goal is to build software that runs on a physical humanoid, I would shortlist these four:

## Humanoid robots with developer SDKs

1. Unitree G1

Public SDK

- Python and C++ SDKs
- ROS 2 support
- Joint and motion control

- Open-source developer repositories

Public SDK

- Locomotion and motion-control development
- Simulation integration

Documentation: [Unitree developer documentation](https://support.unitree.com/home/en/developer/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

3. Booster T1 / T2

Public SDK

- Python SDK
- C++ SDK
- DDS-based communication
